_comment: Preguntas ORIGINALES tipo NIE del capítulo 4.1. No son preguntas reales del examen. Comprueba con tu edición 2027.

questions.scenario: When does a complainant's anonymity under the Sexual Offences (Amendment) Act 1992 begin?
options: When the allegation of the offence is made

questions.scenario: How long does the complainant's anonymity last?
options: Until the end of the trial

questions.scenario: A suspect is arrested for rape but never charged. Does the complainant keep anonymity?
options: Yes – it applies once the allegation is made, whatever the outcome

questions.scenario: A complainant aged 30 wants to waive anonymity to give a TV interview. What is required?
options: A court order in every case
Her written consent, freely given (she must be 16 or over)

questions.scenario: Can a 15-year-old complainant validly consent in writing to being identified?
options: No – the complainant must be 16 or over
explanations: Not under the Act's consent exception ⚠.

questions.scenario: Which of these is most likely a breach of the 1992 Act?
options: Publishing the complainant's street, job and age so locals can identify her
Reporting that 'a woman' was attacked in Hampshire
Naming the convicted defendant in a stranger attack
explanations: Usually lawful unless it identifies the victim.

questions.scenario: Who is protected by statutory lifetime anonymity under the 1992 Act?
What kind of offence is publishing material in breach of the 1992 Act?
Apart from complainant consent, how else may the anonymity restriction be lifted?
options: By a court direction in specified circumstances

questions.scenario: A victim calls police 1 hour after an oral rape. What early-evidence advice is appropriate?
options: Have a drink of water to calm down
Avoid eating, drinking or brushing teeth; use an early evidence kit (mouth swab)

questions.scenario: What is a SARC?
options: Sexual Assault Referral Centre – forensic medical exam and support

questions.scenario: What is the role of an ISVA?
options: Independent Sexual Violence Adviser – supports the victim

questions.scenario: How should a first responder approach the victim's account?
options: Take a full detailed statement at the scene
Obtain a brief initial account; the full account is usually taken later by video-recorded (ABE) interview

questions.scenario: Under YJCEA 1999, how are complainants of sexual offences treated for special measures?
options: Automatically eligible as intimidated witnesses unless they decline

questions.scenario: Can a defendant charged with rape cross-examine the complainant in person?
Under s. 41 YJCEA 1999, evidence about the complainant's sexual behaviour…
options: Cannot be raised without the court's leave, granted only in limited circumstances
Can be raised by police in interview only

questions.scenario: Which special measure lets the complainant's cross-examination be recorded before trial?
Is the SOA 2003 generally gender-neutral?
options: Yes – except rape, which requires penile penetration

questions.scenario: Does the 1992 Act's anonymity cover attempted rape?
options: Yes – attempts, conspiracy and incitement are included

questions.scenario: A journalist didn't know and had no reason to suspect that an allegation had been made. What is the position?
options: A statutory defence may be available

questions.scenario: Which item should usually be seized from the scene in a recent rape allegation?
options: Bedding and clothing worn during the offence

questions.scenario: Which statement about victim-blaming is correct?
options: Officers should avoid victim-blaming and record the account; myths and stereotypes undermine investigations
Questions about clothing help assess credibility

questions.scenario: A complainant reports a rape that happened 10 years ago. What is the correct approach?
options: Investigate – there is no time limit for indictable sexual offences; delayed reporting is common

questions.scenario: Which of these could breach anonymity through 'jigsaw identification'?
options: One outlet names the village, another the victim's school and job

questions.scenario: Under s. 72 SOA 2003 (⚠), offences against children abroad…
options: Can be tried in England & Wales when committed by UK nationals or residents
Only if the other country agrees
